Oregon applicants to the “U visa” program mostly got their applications certified by law enforcement — unless they were in the state's most racially diverse county.

Actual Article Body:
Independent. Member-supported.For the Pacific Northwest.

Independent.Member-supported.

Several years ago, Portland attorney Patrick Sherwood’s client reported to police that she was assaulted as a 17-year-old. She wanted her assailant brought to justice, but as a member of a family at risk for deportation, she was vulnerable. She sought protection by requesting police sign off on a certification for what’s called a U visa application.

In this photo illustration, a U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services I-918 Petition for U Nonimmigrant Status form, known as a U visa, is shown in Hillsboro, Ore., on Sept. 29, 2026.

Eli Imadali / OPB

The United States allows immigrants who are victims of certain crimes to apply for a U visa if they are “helpful” to law enforcement.

In the case of Sherwood’s client, police denied the application twice.

Actual Article Body:
Pope Leo XIV has urged European leaders seeking to end Russia’s war against Ukraine to be ready to make concessions for the sake of peace. He made the remarks yesterday during a visit to France.

“We need to show courage in negotiation and to be willing to give up some positions for the greater good of ​peace,” the pope said, drawing a parallel to a 1917 call by his predecessor Benedict XV during World War I.

The pope did not spell out what he meant by “some positions.”

Leo XIV cautioned European leaders against building up their defense capabilities, saying, “We must also guard against the illusion that rearmament is the answer.” He urged them to ask themselves whether they wanted peace or were simply trying to prepare better for future conflicts.
